exception_rules.heuristic: Check if the process is a recognized cloud CLI or SDK performing standard API calls. If the binary path belongs to standard virtualenvs and the remote IP maps to official cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) or cloud endpoints (*.amazonaws.com, *.googleapis.com), it is likely benign.
Check if standard package managers read local configuration files (e.g., .npmrc or .pip.conf) and connect to official registries (registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org). If so, it is benign.

Check if the package is a dedicated network utility or DNS helper. If the process is doing high-volume resolution of normal domains, it is benign. If it utilizes subdomains encoding base64/hex data to an unknown name server, it is malicious.

Check if a legitimate web framework (Django, Flask, FastAPI) loads a `.env` file during startup and then initiates database connections to local/private network ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x, 192.168.x.x, localhost). If so, mitigate risk as this is standard application initialization.

Verify if the process represents a long-running daemon task (e.g., task worker, celery, redis-server, watchman). If the delayed burst matches standard event-loop callbacks or scheduled cron-like tasks, it is benign.
